thread:
erin: saw a big eviction wave in us-west1 around 22:03 UTC, multiple g4dn-preemptible nodes got reclaimed in the gpu-spot-pool :rotating_light:
jake: yikes — did cluster-autoscaler try to replace them?
priya: CA logged a bunch of `ScaleUp` events but then hit backoff, looks like control-plane API errors at the same time. here's the relevant snippet from the CA pod logs:
```
I0320 22:03:12 scale_up.go:123] Attempting to scale up: gpu-spot-pool replicas=6 -> 10
E0320 22:03:13 kube_client.go:98] API error: 429 Too Many Requests
W0320 22:03:14 backoff.go:45] Backoff: next try in 30s
```
erin: 429 during mass replacement explains why fallback didn't kick in. we also had 3 failed instance creation attempts in the cloud console (quota-ish?).
jake: checked cloud console — quota looks fine, but there were transient failures in the us-west1 GPU SKU provisioning. possibly capacity exhaustion at provider side.
priya: hmm, we have fallback nodepool (gpu-fallback-preemptible) but autoscaler can't move pods because taints/affinity on production pools. we need a short policy tweak to allow spillover for critical routes.
tom: +1, recommend a temporary toleration for `gpu-critical` pods and lower nodeSelector requirements for fallback. pushing a quick kustomize patch now.
erin: also, routing wise we saw higher request fanout to control plane when nodes failed — telemetry shows API QPS spike, adding retry jitter might help. filing an alert for control-plane error rate.
jake: I'm going to increase `--max-node-provision-time` for CA and reduce scale down aggressiveness so we don't oscillate during provider instability.
priya: patch ready: add toleration and relax nodeSelector for `model-infer` daemonset on fallback pool. patch contains this diff:
```yaml
- nodeSelector: {gpu-type: a100}
+ nodeSelector: { }
  tolerations:
+ - key: "gpu-critical"
+   operator: "Exists"
+   effect: "NoSchedule"
```
erin: rolling that now in canary (1/3 clusters). also enabling a temporary autoscaler fallback policy: prefer dedicated baseline pool before throwing 429s to clients.
tom: can we add a 10% reserved capacity in fallback pools for emergencies? would avoid zero-headroom situations.
jake: agree, long-term we should reserve buffer and also add region-handoff policy so we can route to us-east if us-west capacity is down. short-term I enabled 4 reserved preemptible nodes in gpu-fallback-preemptible.
priya: tests look good, pods started on fallback after toleration. latency for some model endpoints spiked but stayed within SLO thanks to graceful fallback.
erin: nice. created a follow-up ticket to update CA config, add provider-capacity-monitoring, and add runbook steps for eviction waves. tagging oncall and infra leads. :white_check_mark:
k8s-bot: Deployment rollout: infer-models-canary — 1/3 -> 3/3 (completed)
erin: thanks all, keep an eye on alert for the next 2 hours and we can revert the relaxed selectors once provider stabilizes.
